scope: Corollary 7.5 (Local boundary variance, independently of ambient size) of the manuscript “Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces on the triangular lattice” (preprints/Uniform-real-Lipschitz-surfaces-on-the-triangular-lattice-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce5ae39087f446a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix nested squares Q0 ⋐ Q1 ⋐ Q2 ⋐ Q3 and positive geometric separation constants. Consider finite triangular-lattice domains of mesh n−1, with arbitrary ambient diameter, fixed data in [−1/2, 1/2], and deterministic sign strings. Suppose a connected observed piece of diameter at least c > 0 lies within bounded distance of Q2. Assume the local hypotheses of 3.1 and 4.1, with constants independent of ambient diameter. Assume also that restricting the observed system to Q3 and adjoining its artificial exterior gives the common mesh thickness constants of Definition 6.1. This holds for connected strands attached to the original exterior, or for components of uniformly positive diameter: cut pieces meeting the artificial boundary join that boundary, and pieces entirely inside are whole original components. For each fixed η > 0, let µn,η be a deterministic smooth probability test supported in Q0, at distance at most Cη from the observed set in Q1. Suppose these measures have a common 1/2-Frostman constant, independent of n, η, and for fixed η their densities range over a compact smooth-test family. If Xn(µ) denotes the Riemann pairing of the centered field with that density, then lim η↓0 lim sup n→∞ sup Var Xn(µn,η) = 0. (7.7) The supremum is over the stated local geometries, tests, and arbitrary ambient domains. The inner limit is always taken at fixed η.
